title: Introduce RBAC anomaly detector, KMS usage ledger, and jurisdictional pin gate
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: customers operating in regulated jurisdictions require stronger evidence about access decisions and KMS usage, plus automated detection of unusual privilege changes. This PR adds three coordinated pieces: 1) an RBAC Anomaly Detector that samples policy decisions and surfaces statistical deviations (new service + control plane telemetry), 2) a KMS Usage Ledger that records per-tenant, per-key KMS call metadata for non-repudiable audit and residency verification, and 3) a Jurisdictional Pin Gate that enforces region-pin policies at the KMS allocation layer and emits canonical audit events for downstream compliance pipelines. The goals are: reduce investigation time for policy breaches, provide provable KMS usage trails for compliance audits, and enforce region pin constraints at the decision point to avoid accidental cross-region key use. Changes in this PR touch: policy evaluation path, audit forwarder, KMS allocation middleware, migrations for the ledger schema, the console telemetry surface, and operator-facing rollout flags. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-9485) - [x] Unit + integration tests for policy sampler - [x] Ledger write path is idempotent and signed - [x] Backwards-compatible migration and feature flag - [x] Console telemetry panels added - [x] e2e scenario for region-pin enforcement (simulated cross-region request) Backwards compatibility: the anomaly detector is opt-in and behind "rbac_anomaly_enabled" feature flag. KMS ledger writes are opt-in per-tenant until a migration window closes. Rollout plan: gradual enablement by tenant cohort, tie ledger writes to audit retention throttles, monitor error rates and key write latency. See commits for incremental scope and the review thread for design clarifications.

review_thread: Liam Nguyen (2025-02-13): Nice direction. Two asks: (1) how do we bound false positives for the anomaly detector so SRE doesn't get paged? (2) ledger writes need to be resilient to transient DB errors. Can you add backoff and non-blocking fallback?

Aisha Patel (2025-02-13): Replied: added exponential backoff + circuit breaker for ledger writes, detector uses an adjustable baseline window and an anomaly-confidence threshold; default is conservative (only P>0.999 alerts). Added config to route low-confidence alerts to a noiseless 'review' stream instead of pages.

Sofia Alvarez (2025-02-14): We need a clear privacy/legal review for storing KMS call metadata. Please ensure tenant opt-in and a data-retention TTL per-tenant. Also: mandate KMS key-id hashing before storing any identifier in non-secure stores.

Aisha Patel (2025-02-15): Replied: implemented per-tenant opt-in flag, retention TTL, and HMAC-prefix hashing of key IDs before writing to ledger. Sensitive raw IDs are only stored in the sealed PostgreSQL column encrypted with CMK; non-sensitive indexes use hashed prefixes.
Marcus Reed (2025-02-16): Test comment: e2e simulated tenant with region pin should reject cross-region KMS allocation and emit a signed audit event; test flaked once in CI (timing).
Aisha Patel (2025-02-16): Flakiness debug: extended the test timeout and added an eventual consistency assertion for the fanout queue. Reran locally and CI.
Liam Nguyen (2025-02-18): Approve after nit fixes.
Sofia Alvarez (2025-02-19): Approve. Note: legal signoff attached to the Linear ticket SEC-223.

release_notes: Added opt-in RBAC anomaly detection service, per-tenant KMS usage ledger for verifiable audit trails, and a jurisdictional pin gate preventing KMS allocations across pinned regions. Feature is behind flags; see docs/compliance/kms_ledger_guide.md for tenant opt-in, retention controls, and migration steps.
